defs.def: a weapon designed to explode at a particular time or when it is dropped or thrown 炸弹

ex.s: Instead, they explode in your mouth like little flavor bombs.
ex.t: 相反，它们在你嘴里像小炸弹一样爆开，充满风味。

defs.def: nuclear weapons (atomic or hydrogen bombs) 核武器；核弹

ex.s: After coming back from the US, Deng devoted himself whole-heartedly to the development of the “two bombs”.
ex.t: 从美国回来后，邓稼先全身心投入到“两弹”的研制中。

ex.s: After the successful development of the atomic bomb, he worked closely with Yu Min, another leading scientist at the cutting edge of nuclear technology.
ex.t: 原子弹研制成功后，他与另一位处于核技术前沿的顶尖科学家于敏密切合作。

ex.s: Together, they thought outside the box and broke new ground, leading to the breakthrough of the hydrogen bomb.
ex.t: 他们一起打破常规、开辟新路，促成了氢弹的突破。

defs.def: a lot of money 很多钱
a complete failure 彻底的失败
a long forward throw of the ball 美式足球
a container in which a liquid such as paint or insect poison is kept under pressure and released as a spray or as foam 气溶胶弹式容器（油漆、杀虫剂等液体加压贮存可喷出）
to attack sb/sth by leaving a bomb in a place or by dropping bombs from a plane 轰炸；对 … 投炸弹

ex.s: Among the many horrors inflicted on humanity by the Second World War was the massive bombing of civilians, often referred to as “terror bombing”.
ex.t: 第二次世界大战给人类带来的诸多恐怖之中，包括对平民的大规模轰炸，常被称为“恐怖轰炸”。

ex.s: One day, the bombing stopped and the  52  left.
ex.t: 有一天，轰炸停止了，____离开了。

ex.s: One soldier recalled how he barely made it with bombs falling all around him: “I was the first one out.
ex.t: 一名士兵回忆起炸弹在四周不断落下、自己勉强逃生的情景：“我是第一个冲出来的。”

defs.def: to move very fast, especially in a vehicle, in a particular direction 快速移动，疾行（尤指乘车）
to fail a test or an exam very badly （考试）惨败
to fail very badly 戏剧、演出等
if you are bombed out, your home is destroyed by bombs （家园）被炸毁；被炸得无家可归
if a building is bombed out, it has been destroyed by bombs （建筑）被炸毁
